title: Explore Your Computer's Hardware
description: Use built-in Windows tools to discover and document your computer's hardware specifications
objective: Students will use Task Manager, System Information, and Device Manager to identify CPU, RAM, storage, and GPU specifications of their own computer

steps.title: Open System Information
steps.instructions:
Press **Win + R**, type `msinfo32`, and press Enter.

In the System Information window, find and write down:
- **OS Name** (e.g., Microsoft Windows 11 Pro)
- **Processor** (e.g., Intel Core i5-12400 @ 2.50GHz)
- **Installed Physical Memory (RAM)** (e.g., 16.0 GB)
- **BaseBoard Manufacturer** (your motherboard brand)

Take a screenshot of this window.

steps.title: Explore Task Manager Performance
steps.instructions:
Press **Ctrl + Shift + Esc** to open Task Manager.

Click the **Performance** tab and explore each section:

1. **CPU** — Note the speed (GHz), cores, logical processors, and current usage %
2. **Memory** — Note total RAM, how much is in use, and available
3. **Disk** — Note if it says SSD or HDD, read/write speeds
4. **GPU** — Note the graphics card name and dedicated memory

Take a screenshot of each section.

steps.title: Check Device Manager
steps.instructions:
Right-click the **Start button** → click **Device Manager** (or press Win + X → M).

Expand these categories and note what's listed:
- **Display adapters** — Your graphics card
- **Network adapters** — WiFi and Ethernet cards
- **Disk drives** — Storage devices
- **Processors** — How many entries (this shows logical cores)

Look for any yellow triangle ⚠️ icons — these mean a driver problem.

Take a screenshot if you find any warnings.

steps.title: Check Storage Health
steps.instructions:
Open **Settings** (Win + I) → **System** → **Storage**.

1. Note total capacity and free space on C: drive
2. Click **Temporary files** — how much space can you reclaim?
3. Click **Show more categories** — what's using the most space?

Now open **Command Prompt** (search 'cmd') and type:
```
wmic diskdrive get model,size,mediaType
```
This shows your exact drive model. Search this model online to confirm if it's SSD or HDD.

steps.title: Create Your System Report
steps.instructions:
Open Command Prompt and run:
```
systeminfo > C:\Users\%USERNAME%\Desktop\my-system-report.txt
```

Open the file from your Desktop. This contains EVERYTHING about your system.

Now create a summary document (Word or Notepad) with:
- Computer name
- OS version
- CPU (name, speed, cores)
- RAM (total, type if visible)
- Storage (type, capacity, free space)
- GPU (name, memory)
- Any issues found (yellow triangles in Device Manager)

**Submit this summary document as your lab report.**

expected_output: A system summary document containing accurate hardware specifications discovered using msinfo32, Task Manager, Device Manager, and systeminfo command
